source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 13 (PDF 291-304), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 13 (Halogens) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 The halogens are the elements of:
(Halogens periodic table ke kis group ke elements hain?)
blocks.explanation: Periodic table ke Group 17 ya VIIA ke elements halogens kehlate hain (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Elements present in Group 17 or VIIA of the periodic table are termed as halogens

blocks.prompt:
2 Which two members of the halogen family are very rare and radioactive?
(Halogen family ke kaun se do members bohat kam milte hain aur radioactive (tabkari) hain?)
blocks.explanation: Pehle chaar halogens aam hain; astatine (At) aur tennessine (Ts) bohat kam milte hain aur radioactive hain (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: astatine (At) and tennessine (Ts) are very rare and radioactive elements

blocks.prompt:
3 In the gas, liquid and solid phases, the halogens exist as:
(Gas, liquid aur solid teeno halaton mein halogens kis shakal mein hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Halogens har halat (gas, liquid ya solid) mein diatomic (do-atomi) molecules X₂ ki shakal mein hote hain (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Halogens exist as diatomic molecules in all phases (gas, liquid or solid)

blocks.prompt:
4 At room temperature bromine is a:
(Room temperature par bromine kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bromine (Br₂) room temperature par surkhi-mayl bhoora (reddish-brown) volatile (jaldi urne wala) liquid hai (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Bromine (Br₂) is a volatile liquid of reddish-brown colour at room temperature

blocks.prompt:
5 On warming, solid iodine changes directly into a:
(Garam karne par solid iodine seedha kis cheez mein badalta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Iodine chamakdar greyish black solid hai jo seedha solid se violet (banafshi) vapour ban jata hai, yani sublime hota hai (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: It sublimes directly from solid to a violet vapor

blocks.prompt:
6 The colour of the halogens from chlorine to iodine:
(Chlorine se iodine tak halogens ka rang kaise badalta hai?)

options.text: darja ba darja gehra hota hai

blocks.explanation: Chlorine se iodine tak halogens ka rang darja ba darja gehra hota jata hai, molecules ke andar electron transitions se light ke absorption (jazb) ki tabdeeli ki wajah se (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: The colors of halogens (X₂) darken progressively from chlorine to iodine

blocks.prompt:
7 The trend of colour change from chlorine to iodine is due to:
(Chlorine se iodine tak rang ki tabdeeli ki wajah kya hai?)

options.text: har molecule mein atoms ki tadaad barhna
molecules ke andar electron transitions se light ke absorption mein tabdeeli

blocks.explanation: Rang ka yeh silsila halogen molecules ke andar electron transitions ki wajah se light ke absorption (jazb) mein tabdeeli se hai (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: due to changes in the absorption of light as a result of electron transitions

blocks.prompt:
8 The first halogen to be isolated and recognised as an element was:
(Sab se pehle kaun sa halogen alag kiya gaya aur element ke taur par pehchana gaya?)
blocks.explanation: 'Did You Know!' box ke mutabiq chlorine pehla halogen tha jise alag kiya gaya aur element maana gaya (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: The first halogen to be isolated and recognized as an element was chlorine

blocks.prompt:
9 The name 'halogen' comes from Greek words meaning:
(Lafz 'halogen' Greek ke jin alfaaz se bana hai un ka matlab hai:)
blocks.explanation: Halogen Greek 'halos' (namak) aur 'gen' (banana) se bana hai, yani namak banane wala (Introduction box).

book_ref.quote: meaning “salt”, and “gen”, meaning “to make.”

blocks.prompt:
10 According to Table 13.1, the outer shell electron configuration of bromine is:
(Table 13.1 ke mutabiq bromine ki outer shell electron configuration kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Table 13.1: F 2s²2p⁵, Cl 3s²3p⁵, Br 4s²4p⁵, I 5s²5p⁵; har halogen ke outer shell mein saat electrons hain (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Outer shell electron configuration

blocks.prompt:
11 Using the relative atomic masses in Table 13.1, the molar mass of an I₂ molecule is:
(Table 13.1 ki relative atomic masses se I₂ molecule ki molar mass kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Iodine ki relative atomic mass 126.9 hai, is liye I₂ = 2 × 126.9 = 253.8 g mol⁻¹ (Table 13.1).

book_ref.quote: Table 13.1 Atomic and Physical properties of the common halogens.

blocks.prompt:
12 Table 13.1 gives the solubility of bromine as 3.6 g per 100 g of water at 20 °C. The mass of bromine that dissolves in 250 g of water at 20 °C is:
(Table 13.1 mein bromine ki solubility 20 °C par 3.6 g fi 100 g paani hai. 250 g paani mein kitna bromine hal hoga?)

book_ref.quote: Solubility/g per 100g of water at 20ºC

blocks.prompt:
13 From the melting and boiling points in Table 13.1, bromine stays a liquid over a temperature range of:
(Table 13.1 ke melting aur boiling points se bromine kitne temperature range mein liquid rehta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bromine -7 °C par pighalta aur 59 °C par ubalta hai, is liye 59 - (-7) = 66 °C ke range mein liquid hai, aur 20 °C par liquid hai (Table 13.1).

book_ref.quote: Physical state at of 20 ºC

blocks.text: 13.1 Volatility of chlorine, bromine and iodine

blocks.prompt:
14 At room temperature, which of chlorine, bromine and iodine is the most volatile and disperses quickly in the air?
(Room temperature par chlorine, bromine aur iodine mein se sab se zyada volatile kaun hai jo hawa mein jaldi phail jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Chlorine room temperature par gas hai (book correction: liquid nahi), is liye teeno mein sab se zyada volatile hai (13.1).

book_ref.quote: At room temperature chlorine is a gas (bromine is the liquid and iodine a solid)

blocks.prompt:
15 Compared with chlorine and iodine, bromine is:
(Chlorine aur iodine ke muqable mein bromine:)

options.text: chlorine se kam lekin iodine se zyada volatile

blocks.explanation: Bromine liquid hone ki wajah se chlorine se kam lekin iodine se zyada volatile hai (13.1).

book_ref.quote: Bromine being a liquid is less volatile than chlorine but more volatile than iodine.

blocks.prompt:
16 The decrease in volatility from chlorine to iodine is due to all of the following EXCEPT:
(Chlorine se iodine tak volatility ke kam hone ki wajah in sab mein se hai SIWAYE:)

options.text: London dispersion forces ka mazboot hona

blocks.explanation: Yeh silsila group mein neeche molecular mass barhne, outer shell ka size barhne aur London dispersion forces mazboot hone se hai; molecular mass barhta hai, kam nahi hota (13.1).

book_ref.quote: This trend is due to the increasing molecular mass, increase in size of outer shell and stronger intermolecular forces

blocks.prompt:
17 Bromine liquid evaporates easily at room temperature, giving off a vapour that is:
(Bromine liquid room temperature par aasani se bukharat banta hai; us ka vapour kaisa hota hai?)

options.text: orange, bohat tez aur buri boo wala
greenish yellow aur meethi boo wala

blocks.explanation: Bromine aasani se urr kar orange vapour deta hai; is ki boo bohat tez aur buri hai, isi liye naam Greek 'bromos' (badboo) se hai (13.1 box).

book_ref.quote: Bromine liquid evaporates easily at room temperatures emitting an orange vapor.

blocks.text: 13.2 Trend in volatility of the halogens

blocks.prompt:
18 The main intermolecular forces that decide the volatility of the halogens are:
(Halogens ki volatility ka faisla karne wali bunyadi intermolecular forces kaun si hain?)
blocks.explanation: Halogens non-polar hain, is liye instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (id-id, London) forces in ki volatility tay karti hain (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Halogens are non-polar and instantaneous dipole-induced forces play a significant role

blocks.prompt:
19 Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces depend on:
(Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces kin cheezon par munhasar hain?)

options.text: molecule ka size, shape aur polarizability

blocks.explanation: Yeh forces molecule ke size, shape aur polarizability (barqi bigaar ki salahiyat) par munhasar hain (13.2).

book_ref.quote: The forces depend on factors like molecular size, shape and polarizability

blocks.prompt:
20 A more volatile substance has:
(Zyada volatile substance ka:)
blocks.explanation: Volatility boiling point ke ulat (inversely) hai; zyada volatile substance ka boiling point kam hota hai (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Volatility is inversely related to the boiling point of a substance.

blocks.prompt:
21 According to Table 13.2, a large molecule of high polarizability has:
(Table 13.2 ke mutabiq zyada polarizability wale bare molecule ki:)

options.text: mazboot id-id forces, zyada boiling point aur kam volatility
kamzor id-id forces, kam boiling point aur zyada volatility
mazboot id-id forces aur zyada volatility
kamzor id-id forces aur zyada boiling point

blocks.explanation: Table 13.2: bara size, zyada polarizability, mazboot id-id forces, zyada boiling point, kam volatility (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces

blocks.prompt:
22 Stronger intermolecular forces give a higher boiling point because:
(Mazboot intermolecular forces se boiling point kyun zyada hota hai?)

options.text: covalent X-X bond tootna zaroori hai
molecules ko liquid se gas phase mein alag karne ke liye zyada energy chahiye

blocks.explanation: Mazboot intermolecular forces mein molecules ko liquid se gas phase mein alag karne ke liye zyada energy chahiye (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Stronger intermolecular forces require more energy to separate the molecules

blocks.prompt:
23 Bromine is a liquid at room temperature while chlorine is a gas because bromine:
(Room temperature par bromine liquid aur chlorine gas kyun hai? Kyunke bromine:)

options.text: chhota hai aur forces kamzor hain
bara hai aur us ki intermolecular forces mazboot hain

blocks.explanation: Bromine liquid hai kyunke us ka size bara hai aur fluorine aur chlorine se mazboot intermolecular forces hain (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Bromine is a liquid as its size is bigger and it possesses stronger intermolecular forces

blocks.prompt:
24 Iodine is a solid at room temperature because it has:
(Iodine room temperature par solid kyun hai?)

options.text: group mein sab se kamzor id-id forces
group ke sab se chhote molecules
group mein sab se mazboot id-id forces

blocks.explanation: Iodine ki intermolecular forces group mein sab se mazboot hain, is liye woh room temperature par solid hai (13.2).

book_ref.quote: Iodine has the strongest forces among the group, so it is in solid state at room temperature.

blocks.prompt:
25 Using Table 13.1, the difference between the boiling points of bromine and chlorine is:
(Table 13.1 se bromine aur chlorine ke boiling points ka farq kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Boiling points: Br₂ 59 °C, Cl₂ -35 °C; farq = 59 - (-35) = 94 °C; bare Br₂ ki London forces mazboot hain (13.2, Table 13.1).

book_ref.quote: Table 13.2 Effect of London forces on physical properties

blocks.text: 13.3 The bond strength of halogen molecules

blocks.prompt:
26 From chlorine to iodine the X-X bond strength decreases because:
(Chlorine se iodine tak X-X bond strength kyun kam hoti hai?)

options.text: atomic size barhta hai, bond lambe aur kamzor hote hain

blocks.explanation: Group mein neeche atomic size barhta hai, is liye bond length lambi aur bond kamzor hota hai (13.3).

book_ref.quote: increase in the atomic size down the group which results in longer bond lengths and weaker bonds

blocks.prompt:
27 The F-F bond is weaker than expected because:
(F-F bond tawaqqo se kamzor kyun hai?)

options.text: fluorine ke lone pairs nahi hote
chhote F atoms ke lone pairs qareeb hote hain aur shadeed electron-electron repulsion hota hai

blocks.explanation: Fluorine atoms bohat chhote hain, is liye dono atoms ke lone pairs mein shadeed repulsion (dhakelna) hota hai jo bond kamzor karta hai (13.3, Fig. 13.1).

book_ref.quote: However, fluorine is an exception in this group.

blocks.prompt:
28 According to Table 13.3, the correct order of bond energy is:
(Table 13.3 ke mutabiq bond energy ki sahi tarteeb kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bond energies: Cl₂ 243, Br₂ 193, F₂ 156, I₂ 151 kJ mol⁻¹, is liye Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂ (Table 13.3).

book_ref.quote: Table 13.3 Bond energies of halogen molecules

blocks.prompt:
29 From Table 13.3, by how much is the bond energy of Cl₂ greater than that of F₂?
(Table 13.3 se Cl₂ ki bond energy F₂ se kitni zyada hai?)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ 243 - F₂ 156 = 87 kJ mol⁻¹ (Table 13.3).

book_ref.quote: Moving from top to bottom in group 17, the bond energy of halogens decreases gradually from chlorine to iodine.

blocks.prompt:
30 Each fluorine atom in the F₂ molecule (Fig. 13.1) carries how many lone pairs of electrons?
(F₂ molecule (Fig. 13.1) mein har fluorine atom par kitne lone pairs hain?)
blocks.explanation: Fluorine ke saat outer electrons hain (2s²2p⁵); aik F-F bond mein lagta hai aur baqi chhe teen lone pairs bante hain (13.3, Fig. 13.1).

book_ref.quote: F2 molecule with lone pairs of electrons

blocks.text: 13.4 Relative reactivities of the halogens as oxidising agents

blocks.prompt:
31 When halogens form ionic compounds with metals, they:
(Jab halogens metals ke saath ionic compounds banate hain to woh:)

options.text: electrons dete hain aur positive ions bante hain
electrons lete hain aur negative halide ions bante hain

blocks.explanation: Metals ke saath ionic compounds banate waqt halogens electrons lete hain aur negative halide ions bante hain, maslan 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl; yeh oxidizing agents hain (13.4).

book_ref.quote: the halogens gain electrons and are converted to negative halide ions

blocks.prompt:
32 The weakest oxidizing agent among the halogens F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂ is:
(F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ aur I₂ mein sab se kamzor oxidizing agent kaun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Oxidizing power group mein neeche kam hoti hai: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; iodine sab se kam hai (13.4).

book_ref.quote: Fluorine has the highest oxidizing power and iodine the least.

blocks.prompt:
33 Chlorine water is added to potassium iodide solution. Which change takes place?
(Potassium iodide solution mein chlorine water dala jata hai. Kya tabdeeli hogi?)

options.text: I⁻ oxidize ho kar I₂ banta hai aur Cl₂ reduce ho kar Cl⁻
Cl⁻ oxidize ho kar Cl₂ banta hai
I₂ reduce ho kar I⁻ banta hai

blocks.explanation: Chlorine Br⁻ aur I⁻ ko oxidize karke displace kar sakta hai: Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂ (13.4).

book_ref.quote: Similarly, chlorine can oxidize and displace Br⁻ and I⁻.

blocks.prompt:
34 Which mixture shows NO reaction?
(Kis mixture mein koi reaction NAHI hoga?)
blocks.explanation: Halogen sirf apne neeche wale halide ions ko displace karta hai; iodine kisi halide ion ko oxidize nahi kar sakta, is liye I₂ + Br⁻ mein reaction nahi (13.4).

book_ref.quote: Iodine cannot oxidize any halide ion.

blocks.prompt:
35 Bromine can oxidize and displace:
(Bromine kis ko oxidize karke displace kar sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bromine sirf I⁻ ko oxidize karke displace kar sakta hai jo us ke neeche hai (13.4).

book_ref.quote: Bromine can oxidize and displace I⁻.

blocks.prompt:
36 In the balanced equation for fluorine displacing chloride ions, one F₂ molecule reacts with:
(Fluorine ke chloride ions ko displace karne ki balanced equation mein aik F₂ molecule kitne ions se react karta hai?)

options.text: aik Cl⁻ ion se, aik F⁻ ion
do Cl⁻ ions se, do F⁻ ions aur aik Cl₂ banta hai
chaar Cl⁻ ions se, do Cl₂
aik Cl⁻ ion se, aik Cl₂

blocks.explanation: Balanced (book correction): F₂(g) + 2Cl⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + Cl₂(g); aik F₂ se do fluoride ions bante hain (13.4).

book_ref.quote: The balanced equations are F₂(g) + 2Cl¹⁻(aq) → 2F¹⁻(aq) + Cl₂(g)

blocks.prompt:
37 The standard electrode potentials E° (X₂/X⁻) of the halogens from fluorine to iodine:
(Fluorine se iodine tak halogens ke E° (X₂/X⁻) ki qeemat:)

options.text: kam positive hoti hai, yani oxidizing power kam hoti hai
chlorine ke baad negative ho jati hai

blocks.explanation: E° F₂ (+2.87 V) se I₂ (+0.54 V) tak kam positive hoti hai, jo kam hoti oxidizing power dikhati hai (13.4, Table 13.4).

book_ref.quote: become less positive from fluorine to iodine

blocks.prompt:
38 Using Table 13.4, the difference between the E° values of Cl₂ and Br₂ is:
(Table 13.4 se Cl₂ aur Br₂ ki E° values ka farq kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: E°(Cl₂) = +1.36 V, E°(Br₂) = +1.07 V; farq = 1.36 - 1.07 = 0.29 V; chlorine zyada taqatwar oxidizing agent hai (Table 13.4).

book_ref.quote: Table 13.4 Standard electrode potential E° (X₂/X⁻)

blocks.prompt:
39 A halogen will have high oxidizing power if it has:
(Kisi halogen ki oxidizing power zyada hogi agar us ki:)

options.text: zyada dissociation energy aur kam electron affinity
kam dissociation energy, zyada electron affinity aur ions ki zyada hydration energy
kam electron affinity aur kam hydration energy
zyada dissociation energy aur kam hydration energy

blocks.explanation: Kam dissociation energy, zyada electron affinity aur ions ki zyada hydration energy wala halogen zyada oxidizing power rakhta hai (13.4).

book_ref.quote: A halogen having low energy of dissociation, high electron affinity and higher hydration energy of its ions, will have a high oxidizing power.

blocks.prompt:
40 The heat of vaporization is listed as a factor in the oxidizing power of only:
(Oxidizing power ke factors mein heat of vaporization sirf kin ke liye di gayi hai?)
blocks.explanation: Factors: dissociation energy, electron affinity, hydration energy aur heat of vaporization (Br₂ aur I₂ ke liye), jo room temperature par gas nahi hain (13.4).

book_ref.quote: energy of dissociation, electron affinity of atoms, hydration energies of ions, and heats of vaporization

blocks.text: 13.5 Reactions of the halogens with hydrogen

blocks.prompt:
41 Hydrogen halides are:
(Hydrogen halides kya hain?)

options.text: rangeen liquids jo paani mein hal nahi hote
be-rang gases jo paani mein hal ho kar hydrohalic acids banati hain
safed solids jo paani mein base banate hain
rangeen gases jo paani mein hal nahi hoti

blocks.explanation: Hydrogen halides be-rang gases hain jo paani mein hal ho kar hydrohalic acids banati hain (13.5).

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen halides are colourless gases that dissolve in water to form hydrohalic acid.

blocks.prompt:
42 Fluorine reacts with hydrogen:
(Fluorine hydrogen ke saath kaise react karta hai?)

options.text: sirf catalyst ke saath garam karne par
dhamake se, kam temperature aur andhere mein bhi

blocks.explanation: Kam temperature aur andhere mein bhi fluorine hydrogen se dhamake (explosively) se react karta hai: H₂ + F₂ → 2HF (13.5).

book_ref.quote: At low temperature and in the dark, fluorine reacts explosively with hydrogen.

blocks.prompt:
43 The condition needed for chlorine to react readily with hydrogen is:
(Chlorine ko hydrogen se aasani se react karne ke liye kya shart chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: UV light ya spark (chingari) ki mojoodgi mein chlorine hydrogen se aasani se react karke be-rang HCl gas banata hai (13.5).

book_ref.quote: In the presence of UV light or a spark, chlorine reacts readily with hydrogen

blocks.prompt:
44 Bromine reacts with hydrogen to form HBr:
(Bromine hydrogen ke saath HBr kab banata hai?)

options.text: garam karne par, exothermic reaction mein

blocks.explanation: Garam karne par bromine hydrogen se react karke HBr banata hai; yeh exothermic (heat dene wala) reaction hai (13.5).

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen bromide (HBr) gas is produced when bromine reacts with the hydrogen upon heating.

blocks.prompt:
45 The reaction H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) is:
(Reaction H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) kaisa hai?)

options.text: UV light mein tez aur irreversible
room temperature par catalyst ke baghair mukammal
reversible aur bohat aahista, zyada temperature aur catalyst ke saath

blocks.explanation: Iodine zyada temperature par catalyst ke saath hydrogen se react karta hai; reaction reversible hai aur bohat aahista hota hai (13.5).

book_ref.quote: This is a reversible reaction and occurs very slowly.

blocks.prompt:
46 Using Table 13.1 and H = 1, the mass of HCl formed when 7.1 g of chlorine reacts completely with hydrogen (H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl) is:
(Table 13.1 aur H = 1 le kar, 7.1 g chlorine hydrogen se poori tarah react kare (H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl) to kitni HCl banegi?)

book_ref.quote: When halogen elements react with hydrogen, they produce hydrogen halides.

blocks.prompt:
47 The halogen that needs the most severe conditions (high temperature and a catalyst) to react with hydrogen is:
(Hydrogen se react karne ke liye sab se sakht shiraait (zyada temperature aur catalyst) kis halogen ko chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: Hydrogen ke saath reactivity fluorine se iodine tak kam hoti hai; iodine ko zyada temperature aur catalyst chahiye (13.5).

book_ref.quote: When we move down the group from fluorine to iodine, the reactivity of halogens with hydrogen decreases.

blocks.text: 13.6 Relative thermal stabilities of hydrogen halides in terms of their bond strength

blocks.prompt:
48 The order of thermal stability of the hydrogen halides is:
(Hydrogen halides ki thermal stability ki tarteeb kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Group mein neeche bond dissociation energy kam hone se thermal stability kam hoti hai: HF > HCl > HBr > HI (13.6).

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen fluoride (HF) is the most thermally stable hydrogen halide.

blocks.prompt:
49 The H-F bond is very strong because:
(H-F bond bohat mazboot kyun hai?)

options.text: fluorine ka atomic radius bara hai
fluorine ki zyada electronegativity aur chhota radius mazboot orbital overlap dete hain

blocks.explanation: Fluorine ki zyada electronegativity aur chhota atomic radius orbitals ka mazboot overlap dete hain, is liye H-F bond bohat mazboot hai (13.6).

book_ref.quote: a strong overlap of orbitals produces a very strong H-F bond

blocks.prompt:
50 From Table 13.5, the difference between the bond dissociation energies of H-F and H-I is:
(Table 13.5 se H-F aur H-I ki bond dissociation energies ka farq kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: H-F 569 - H-I 299 = 270 kJ mol⁻¹ (Table 13.5).

book_ref.quote: Table 13.5 Bond dissociation energy of H-X bonds

blocks.prompt:
51 The bond dissociation energy of H-Br given in the chapter is:
(Chapter mein H-Br ki bond dissociation energy kitni di gayi hai?)
blocks.explanation: H-Br: 366 kJ mol⁻¹; bromine ke bare radius aur kam orbital overlap ki wajah se H-F aur H-Cl se kamzor (13.6).

book_ref.quote: Its bond dissociation energy is 366 kJ/mol.

blocks.prompt:
52 HI is the least thermally stable hydrogen halide because:
(HI sab se kam thermally stable hydrogen halide kyun hai?)

options.text: iodine sab se zyada electronegative halogen hai
HI ka H-X bond sab se mazboot hai
iodine sab se chhota halogen hai
bare iodine atom ka kamzor orbital overlap aur sab se kamzor H-X bond

blocks.explanation: Iodine ka bohat bara radius kamzor orbital overlap deta hai, is liye H-I bond sab se kamzor (299 kJ mol⁻¹) hai (13.6).

book_ref.quote: Atomic radius of iodine is very large leading to poor orbital overlap

blocks.prompt:
53 From Table 13.5, how much more energy is needed to break one mole of H-Cl bonds than one mole of H-Br bonds?
(Table 13.5 se aik mole H-Cl bonds todne ke liye aik mole H-Br bonds se kitni zyada energy chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: 431 - 366 = 65 kJ fi mole; HCl HBr se zyada thermally stable hai (13.6).

book_ref.quote: Its bond dissociation energy is 431 KJ/mol.

blocks.text: 13.7 Relative reactivity of halide ions as reducing agents

blocks.prompt:
54 The weakest reducing agent among the halide ions is:
(Halide ions mein sab se kamzor reducing agent kaun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Reducing power: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻; fluoride sab se kamzor reducing agent hai (13.7).

book_ref.quote: Fluoride ion is the weakest reducing agent while iodide is the strongest reducing agent among the halides.

blocks.prompt:
55 The reducing ability of halide ions increases down the group mainly because:
(Group mein neeche halide ions ki reducing ability kyun barhti hai?)

options.text: electronegativity barhti aur radius kam hota hai
electronegativity kam hoti hai aur atomic radius barhta hai
ions mein protons zyada barhte hain

blocks.explanation: Electronegativity kam aur atomic radius zyada hone se charge density kam hoti hai aur electron dena aasan hota hai (13.7).

book_ref.quote: decreasing electronegativity and increasing atomic radius down the group

blocks.prompt:
56 The fluoride ion has little tendency to lose an electron because of its:
(Fluoride ion electron dene ka kam rujhan kyun rakhta hai?)

options.text: bara size aur kam charge density
chhota size aur zyada charge density

blocks.explanation: Chhote fluoride ion ki charge density zyada hai aur fluorine apne extra electron ko mazbooti se pakarta hai, is liye F⁻ electron mushkil se deta hai (13.7).

book_ref.quote: The small size of fluoride ion results in a high charge density

blocks.prompt:
57 Compared with the chloride ion, the bromide ion is:
(Chloride ion ke muqable mein bromide ion:)

options.text: zyada taqatwar reducing agent, bara radius aur kam charge density
kamzor reducing agent, zyada charge density

blocks.explanation: Br⁻ ka ionic radius bara aur charge density kam hai, is liye woh Cl⁻ se aasani se electron deta hai (13.7).

book_ref.quote: Bromide ion (Br⁻) has a larger ionic radius and lower charge density

blocks.prompt:
58 Which statement about the chloride ion as a reducing agent is correct?
(Chloride ion ke reducing agent hone ke baare mein kaun sa bayan durust hai?)

options.text: yeh sab se taqatwar halide reducing agent hai

blocks.text: 13.10 Reactions of chlorine with cold and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide

blocks.explanation: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O. Cl₂ ke moles = 14.2/71.0 = 0.2 mol = NaClO ke moles; mass = 0.2 × 74.5 = 14.9 g (13.10.1).
